What reading lazy data will cost

Source: R/plan.R
nd_plan.Rd

Works out what a read of lazy data (from open_dataset(), after any sel() or isel()) would touch, without reading it: the selection's size, the source chunks it needs, and with the zaro engine the requests, bytes, hosts and transports, from zaro::zaro_plan(). Call it before collect() on something large or remote.

Usage

nd_plan(x, ..., max_chunks = getOption("ndr.plan_max_chunks", 1e+05))

Arguments

x

a Variable, DataArray or Dataset.

...

unused.

max_chunks

the most chunks to plan byte references for: above this, only the counts are given (a whole large array can have millions of chunks). Default getOption("ndr.plan_max_chunks", 1e5).

Value

An nd_plan (printed as a summary). For a Variable or DataArray, a list with var, engine, lazy, selection (the selected sizes of the source dims), values, chunks (touched), chunks_total, chunk_shape, chunk_values (values in the touched chunks), and with the zaro engine requests, bytes (known), unknown_size, hosts, transport and refs (the zaro::zaro_plan() table). For a Dataset, a data frame with one row per data variable.

Details

With the GDAL engine the chunks are GDAL's block size and the requests are not estimated (they depend on the driver). In-memory data has nothing to read.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ds <- open_dataset("https://host/store.zarr", engine = "zaro")
ds$temp |> sel(time = "2023-01-01") |> nd_plan()
nd_plan(ds)
} # }
